clue.text: Spirit with peculiar pill tests family in fairytale

definitions.note: points to a character found in a fairytale rather than naming one

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd or out of the normal order, so the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A drink plus drug-testing kits and relatives somehow turn up in a fairytale.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is the spinning imp of the Grimm brothers' story, so he is someone met in a fairytale.

clue.text: Little lad with nothing claimed by disease of glands

indicators.note: what is claimed by something is taken into it, so the lad and nothing sit inside the disease

parts.note: the immune-deficiency disease
Den is a short form of the boy's name Dennis
zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A small boy with nothing to his name is struck by a glandular illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little lad' means a shortened boy's name, and 'of glands' trails the wordplay so the definition sits at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are lymphatic tissue masses at the back of the nose, commonly called glands.

clue.text: Cost of puppy's first food

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: opening letter of puppy
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: Asking how much it costs to feed a young dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Price and cost are synonyms for the amount charged for something.

clue.text: Clergyman always turns up right before death!

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: ever means always
standard abbreviation for right
one's end is one's death

explanation.surface: The vicar is ever-present at the deathbed, arriving just before someone dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places R ahead of END.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title and informal name for a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Stand after drug-fuelled experience leads to overdose?

indicators.note: one thing leading to another puts the first in front of the second

parts.note: a trip is a hallucinogenic experience
common abbreviation for overdose

explanation.surface: A warning that getting high may end in an overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand for a camera or similar instrument.

clue.text: Recounted heroic exploit about special key

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the heroic exploit wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a deed is a notable act
S is an abbreviation for special
a crib is a key or set of answers used to cheat

explanation.surface: Someone told of a brave feat involving an unusual key.
explanation.walkthrough: DE(S CRIB)ED; a crib, like a key, gives the answers.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to give an account of it, so described means recounted.

clue.text: Threaded saint on crossbar

parts.note: standard abbreviation for saint
a rung is a crossbar of a ladder

explanation.surface: A holy figure strung up on a crossbar like a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works as 'next to', the usual down-clue sense of one piece sitting on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Beads that are strung have had a thread passed through them, so strung means threaded.

clue.text: Veil irony and target's confused by how question is asked

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up, so all the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; the 's is 'is', joining fodder to indicator

explanation.surface: Someone muddled by veils, irony and targets is puzzled by the questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrogatively is the adverb meaning in the manner of a question, describing how something is asked.

clue.text: A rude Wren dancing in bloomers?

definitions.note: an example of the answer, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky Wren, a member of the women's naval service, dancing in her knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service; bloomers are baggy knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are an old-fashioned style of women's knickers, one kind of underwear.

clue.text: Vanquished, beheaded and devoured

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the top, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: beaten means defeated

explanation.surface: A grim fate: defeated, decapitated and then consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devoured has been eaten up greedily; the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Harshly criticise Long for sense of style

parts.note: to pan a show is to review it harshly
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A critic slams someone called Long for their flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is capitalised to look like a surname; it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and stylishness, a flair for doing things with style.

clue.text: Imagine old Briton by river

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Invites you to picture an ancient Briton standing at a riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form an image of it in the mind, which is to imagine it.

clue.text: Put down backward, abbreviated, variety of language

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the shortened word from right to left
something abbreviated is shortened, so the word loses its ending

parts.note: a dialect is a regional variety of a language

explanation.surface: Reads like a scornful note on a slow, clipped form of speech being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: DIALECT shortened to DIAL, then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, so something laid has been put down.

clue.text: Double for inactive campanologist

parts.note: dead means inactive or not working
a campanologist is a bell-ringer

explanation.surface: Seeking a stand-in for a bell-ringer who no longer turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is someone who looks exactly like another person, an identical double.

clue.text: Animal queen put into cabbage dish

indicators.note: what is put into something ends up inside it, so these pieces go within the cabbage

parts.note: cole is an old name for cabbage, as in coleslaw
a donkey
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: Odd recipe: an animal and a queen stuffed into a cabbage dish.
explanation.walkthrough: C(ASS ER)OLE; 'cabbage dish' looks like one phrase but the definition is just 'dish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a stew slow-cooked in the oven, and also the dish it is cooked in.

clue.text: Madame who modelled us a stud?

definitions.note: a title standing for the person who bore it

indicators.note: modelled means shaped into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether the famous waxwork maker made a model of a hunky man for us.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Tussaud made wax figures, so 'modelled' fits both her trade and the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Tussaud, founder of the London waxworks museum, is universally known as Madame Tussaud.

clue.text: Scruffy creature from meadow born into drudgery

indicators.note: into places the preceding pieces inside the word for drudgery

parts.note: fag is British slang for tiring drudgery
lea is a poetic word for meadow
abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A tatty animal emerges from fields into a life of toil.
explanation.walkthrough: F(LEA B)AG; in British usage a fag is a chore or tiresome effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleabag is an informal term for a dirty, unkempt person or animal.

clue.text: Pays for those engaged to receive knight

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so the knight goes inside

parts.note: fiancés are people engaged to be married
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Engaged couples taking in a knight and settling the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: FI(N)ANCES; N, not K, is the knight, because K is already the king in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance something is to provide the money for it, so finances means pays for.

clue.text: Want liberal to enter appeal for strike-breaker

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it, so these pieces sit within the appeal

parts.note: to beg is to appeal earnestly
want in the sense of lack
abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A political-sounding plea about striking workers and liberal intervention.
explanation.walkthrough: B(LACK L)EG; 'Want' means lack, not desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackleg is a derogatory British term for a worker who carries on working during a strike.

clue.text: Musician fingers this and, troubled, turns legit

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed, so the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A troubled musician gives up shady dealings and goes straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutestring is one of the strings of a lute, which the player presses and plucks with the fingers.

clue.text: Copper trailing vehicle uncovers immoral women

indicators.note: trailing means following behind, so copper comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a street vehicle running on rails
P stands for penny, a copper coin

indicators.note: read loosely as exposing just the final letter of its own word

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A policeman following a car exposes women of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is a penny, P. TRAM and P give TRAMP; the final S is loosely clued, most plausibly the last letter of 'uncovers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramp is a dated, offensive term for a promiscuous woman, so tramps are immoral women.

clue.text: Vegetable artist's good-looker

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician; the 's means 'has', joining the pieces
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A painter's handsome partner is compared to a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp red root eaten raw in salads, so it is a vegetable.

clue.text: Large soprano in large tank?

indicators.note: in places the soprano inside the word for the tank

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A hefty soprano singing from inside a big tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second belongs with 'tank' in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast means immense, very large in size or extent.

clue.text: Wait for a proposal by partner

parts.note: taken as written
a bid is an offer or proposal
in bridge, East is the partner of West

explanation.surface: Waiting for a marriage proposal from one's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places the bid next to the partner; E comes from bridge, where East and West play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Abide has an old sense of awaiting or waiting for, as in abiding someone's coming.

clue.text: Frightened to admit king is disfigured

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the king goes inside

parts.note: scared means frightened
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone too afraid to confess the king has been maimed.
explanation.walkthrough: SCA(R)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarred skin bears marks from wounds, so a scarred face has been disfigured.

clue.text: Author with a book out in Nevada

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NV is the postal abbreviation for Nevada

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer with a new book published while staying in Nevada.
explanation.walkthrough: N(ABOKO)V; Nabokov wrote Lolita, partly set on American road trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Urge student to follow setter's fitness programme

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the student goes at the end

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, and the 's is 'is': I'M
PE is physical education
L for learner

explanation.surface: A student is pushed to join the setter's exercise class.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'setter's fitness programme' as 'I'm PE'; L is the learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or push them to act, which is to urge them.

clue.text: Mutant weed, in time, produces flower

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the word for time

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

indicators.note: a mutant has changed form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's tale: a weed mutates and eventually bursts into bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: SP(EEDW)ELL; the joke is that the speedwell is itself often treated as a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small plant of the veronica genus bearing little blue flowers.
